subject: Saw you're hiring a patient coordinator — a thought on missed calls
body:
Hi Edward,

I noticed you're hiring a patient coordinator for the front desk — so this is clearly on your mind. I run a small studio that builds AI phone receptionists for practices like yours, and I wanted to share a quick idea, not a hard pitch.

A front-desk hire is the right move for in-office care — but no single person can catch every call. When your coordinator is checking a patient in, on the other line, or gone for the day (you're closed evenings and weekends), those calls go to voicemail — and a lot of new-patient calls just hang up and dial the next office.

What we build sits alongside your front desk: an AI receptionist that answers every call 24/7 in a natural voice, books and reschedules appointments straight into your system, verifies basics, and only routes the calls that actually need a human. Your coordinator handles the people in the chair; the AI makes sure no call — especially after-hours new-patient calls — ever goes unanswered.

For most offices it costs a fraction of another salary and pays for itself on a couple of recovered new patients a month.

If it's useful, I'm happy to do a quick 10-minute call or even set up a live demo line you can call yourself to hear it. No pressure either way.

Best,
